tasks.title: Railway line feature integration: cell workflow skips, ownership, backup, undo
tasks.notes:
GOAL. Make the railway line a real, journalled FEATURE in the normal cell workflow: skip fast when there is nothing to do, build from the planner's plan with a structure backup, own its footprint so later passes leave it alone, and undo cleanly.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 2, 3, 5 to 8, 10, and "Not in the normal workflow yet"); GLOSSARY.md (Element, Feature); rules/handoff-layered-passes.md (sections 1, 3, 4 and 11: pass order, masks, undo, cross-cell effects); rules/feature-builds.md; lib/journal/cell_features.py and lib/journal/cell_journal.py (how a feature and its footprint are recorded); scripts/cell_registry.py (`propose_feature_candidates`, readiness); lib/site/site_kit.py (`apply`, `_structure_backup`, structure backups, readback); lib/site/element_undo.py; lib/builds/feature_build.py (how a feature spec in site/builds/<name>.json works); the planner (lib/builds/railway_plan.py) and evidence (lib/sources/railway_evidence.py) modules; docs/plans/railway-prototype/rail_apply.py.txt and rail_verify.py.txt.

DECISIONS YOU MUST HONOUR (owner, 2026-11-22):
- PER-CELL WORKFLOW: a cell with no railway is skipped at once. A cell already covered by an earlier railway feature is skipped at once ("marked already by a nearby cell that was done first"). Otherwise plan a railway feature starting from that cell, 2048 x 2048 box, join records at box cuts.
- The feature OWNS its whole footprint: rails, ballast, slopes, planting. The cell trees and decor passes never place inside it (the rules already say a major feature wins; check this holds for railway footprints and enforce it if not), and the ground layer yields to it. Where a road crosses, the feature lays the road surface itself.
- The feature's gaps (crossings, bridges, tunnels) and joins are recorded in the feature record so the crossing-feature ticket can read them.
- BEST EFFORT, FAIL LOUDLY: if the plan has any `failures`, stop BEFORE any block is written and print them. A human fixes those bits.
- Powered rail with a torch two blocks below, corners plain, junctions untouched.

BUILD:
1. Feature proposal for railway in the per-cell flow (propose, prepare, readiness), with the two instant skips.
2. A spec in site/builds/ (name `railway_<tx>_<tz>`) that points at the plan or embeds it, validated by the registry check.
3. Apply through site_kit.apply: structure backup tiles, fills and rail writes, journalled ownership of every footprint column, and a READ-BACK that rescans what was written and RETRIES misses. The trial's first powered-rail pass missed 45 cells (39 rails, 6 torches) near MC x 7376 to 7414 and a retry fixed them; the cause was never found, so treat a miss as normal and retry, then fail loudly if it persists.
4. Undo through the existing element undo, restoring the structure backup and clearing the journal ownership. Covered-cell marking must be undone too.
5. Docs: a railway section in rules/feature-builds.md; GLOSSARY.md note that a railway line is a feature, not a layer.

ACCEPTANCE (tests with MemoryBlocks and the journal test kit, no live server; run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <your test stems>`): proposing for a cell with no railway returns nothing; proposing for a cell covered by an existing railway feature returns nothing; a planned feature applies into MemoryBlocks and the journal shows ownership of every footprint column; a later trees or decor pass over the cell writes nothing inside the footprint; read-back detects a deliberately dropped block and the retry restores it; a persistent miss fails loudly; a plan with failures writes no block at all; undo restores MemoryBlocks exactly; two features on adjacent boxes carry matching join records.

DO NOT: apply to the live world, run a real-place build, or design crossings/bridges/tunnels (their own tickets). If you want a live smoke test, stop and leave it to the real-stretch trial ticket.
WORKFLOW: task/* branch, ship-branch skill. builderTask false. This changes journal ownership across layers, so it is a stretch under docs/agents/model-and-effort.md: ask the owner before raising model or effort.

Shared seams (housekeeping review, docs/plans/housekeeping-review.md): use cellmath, the shared builder helpers (#407) and world-provider roles (#393) rather than new private tables or imports.

tasks.title: Crossing feature mechanism: spec, join records, not-ready gate and crossing builder
tasks.notes:
GOAL. The shared mechanism for crossing, bridge and tunnel features: a spec format, the join records that tie them to railway line features, the "not ready" gate, and a builder for a level crossing driven by a spec. Claude designs each crossing from evidence in a later ticket; this ticket makes that possible.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 7, 9, 10, 11); docs/plans/bridges-and-tunnels.md ("Already decided"); lib/builds/feature_build.py (feature spec pattern in site/builds/<name>.json); lib/blocks/block_reference.py (block id validation); lib/journal/cell_features.py; the line feature module from the integration ticket (its gap and join records); lib/sources/ground_sources.py (road width and surface kinds).

DECISIONS YOU MUST HONOUR (owner, 2026-11-22):
- Each level crossing, bridge and tunnel is its own FEATURE and MAY include rail lines. It records which abutting railway features it joins (cell, level, direction, tracks).
- It is built AFTER the line features and REFUSES ("not ready", exit non-zero, nothing written) until both abutting line features exist in the journal. The line features leave a gap and write end records; this builder reads them.
- The rail feature trumps the road: at a level crossing this feature lays the road surface across the rails itself, using road data, and the rails through at the recorded level (straight cells powered with a torch two blocks below, as in the line feature).
- Gates, lights and bell exist only where the spec says, and the spec's flags come from the OSM tags (`crossing:barrier`, `crossing:light`, `crossing:bell`). Their style and colours are chosen by Claude from Street View in the crossing's own build (a later ticket), so the spec must carry free block ids for bars, posts and lamps, validated against block_reference.py, plus a field for the evidence references (frame ids).
- No default-style fallback and no separate survey: a crossing with no spec is not built.

BUILD:
1. Spec schema (JSON in site/builds/, name `crossing_<tx>_<tz>_<n>`): kind (crossing now; bridge and tunnel only reserve the header), abutting line feature ids and join records, road way ids and surface, rail tracks, barrier/light/bell flags with block ids and positions, evidence references. Document the schema in the module docstring and rules/feature-builds.md. Validate it in the registry check (registry_verify.check_feature_specs).
2. The "not ready" gate and the join-record reader.
3. The crossing builder: road surface across, rails at the join level (reuse the line feature's rail and powered-rail rules, do not copy them), barriers, lights, bell marker; journalled ownership of its footprint; structure backup; read-back with retry; undo.
4. Bridge and tunnel: only the shared header, join reading and gate. Their geometry waits for the bridge and tunnel decisions ticket.

ACCEPTANCE (MemoryBlocks, synthetic specs; no live server): a valid crossing spec builds into MemoryBlocks with rails continuous across the road at the recorded level; with both neighbours missing or only one present the builder refuses and writes nothing; a spec whose block id is not a valid block is rejected; a spec with no barrier flag builds no gates; flags that disagree with the OSM tags recorded in the spec's evidence are rejected; undo restores MemoryBlocks exactly; the registry check reports a malformed spec.

DO NOT: choose real colours or styles (the Claude crossing ticket does), build a real crossing, apply to the live world, or implement bridge or tunnel geometry.
WORKFLOW: task/* branch, ship-branch skill. builderTask false.

Shared seams (housekeeping review, docs/plans/housekeeping-review.md): use cellmath and the barrier vocabulary module (#398) rather than new private tables.

tasks.title: Find what triggers Minecraft rate-limit waits during applies
tasks.notes:
From the 2026-11-21 B35 rebuild thread. The same plan applied four times: fill stage took 122 s with 1 rate-limit retry, 605 s with 10, 485 s with 7, 125 s with 0 (each retry is a fixed 'Minecraft rate limit: retrying in 60s' wait). Unknown what triggers it. One unverified guess: other Minecraft MCP calls (teleport, scan, capture) from a parallel session while an apply runs. Spike: log request timestamps and the server's limit response during an apply, run once with no other calls and once with background calls, and record the limit, whether it is per second or per window, and whether the writer's pacing (see McpWriter, the paced MCP interval in rules/slow-commands.md) can stay under it. Output: a short finding in docs/ with numbers, and either a tuned pacing constant or a filed fix. Acceptance: the finding states the limit and the cause with measurements.

Wave investigation 2026-11-22: partial measured findings at docs/plans/minecraft-rate-limit.md. Installed limiter behavior and 60-second Retry-After are reproduced; current config files say 600 RPM but loaded/historical quotas and the original apply cause need measured traces. tasks.title: Typology generator: accept rotated and irregular footprints, rows by adjacency, front from nearest street
tasks.notes:
From trial #257, findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md (sections "Where the shipped generator stops" and Recommendation 1). The #413 generator refused every real footprint as "odd footprint": 0 of 18 estate, 42 terrace and 42 parade buildings produced a spec, because _box accepts only filled axis-aligned rectangles and real streets are rotated (bounding-box fill 0.29 to 0.94). house_build already fits rotated rectangles (#415) and feature_build takes the footprint as drawn. Change lib/builds/typology_spec.py: (a) accept any footprint of a minimum area and leave the fit to the builder, still reporting a needs-designer reason for slivers and multi-part shapes; (b) form rows from footprints within one block of each other, not a full shared side (_relation, _mark_partial, _components); (c) choose a front from the nearest street when the two axes are close (_front, the shop parade sits on a diagonal road), reporting no-clear-front only when no street is within reach. Colocated tests with fixtures cut from the real Begonia Road, Northcote Road and Portswood Road footprints (record them as small JSON fixtures). Non-builder: synthetic fixtures and unit tests only. Does not touch the district profile or tag defaults (see the tag-defaults task).


Parade verdict addition (2026-11-22, snag S-110, owner decision): do not square shop fronts into steps on a row that is not close to axis-aligned (the squaring directive in rules/craftsmanship.md); the generator should keep the real angle and let the builder fit it, and mark a front 'needs designer' where it cannot. The owner has given up that directive for such rows.

tasks.title: Typology generator: default storeys from the profile, lidar check advisory, class-default fallback for a missing district profile
tasks.notes: From trial #257 (docs/plans/typology-buildings.md, Recommendation 1 and 2). On the study streets building:levels was present on 0 of 18 estate and 0 of 42 terrace buildings and 6 of 42 parade buildings, roof:shape on 0, 0 and 1. The generator refuses on missing building:levels, then on the lidar agreement check, then on no district profile. Change lib/builds/typology_spec.py so a missing building:levels takes the profile class storeys (default from storeys.min when min and max agree, else needs-designer with a clear reason), the lidar height check is advisory (reported in the spec notes, never a refusal, and missing lidar is not a refusal), and a missing district profile falls back to the land-use class default (ADR 006) with the fallback named in the spec note. Observed tags still win. Non-builder: fixtures and unit tests. Independent of the footprint-gates task. The world itself still needs real district profile files (site/districts/*.json) before a rule route gives a district palette: that is world work (profile from the aerial), not a tool task, and the world currently has none.

tasks.title: house_build: roof underlay block sits in the wall's top course (roof material one layer low)
tasks.notes: From trial #257 (docs/plans/typology-buildings.md, "Roof layer"). The owner says the roof material appears to be applied one layer below the roof on the rule-built Begonia Road and Northcote Road houses. Likely cause, to confirm first: house_build.roof() adds a two-layer skin, setting a full block of the roof material at y - 1 under every non-eave pitched cell (self.set(x, y - 1, z, family_variants(rm)['full'])); cells beside the eave sit at the wall-top level, so that block lands in the wall's top course. A live scan of the west semi at x 6347, z -6134..-6123 found full deepslate_tiles at y 63 and y 64 where the top wall course should be brick. First step is a diagnosis against a dry-run plan (compare the planned top course with the wall material); then keep the wall's top course in wall material and seal the stair cutouts without it, or move the underlay below the wall top. Affects house_build pitched roofs (roof_pitch above 0.5) in both the rule-built and hand-spec path; check whether feature_build pitched roofs have the same extra layer. Tests with a synthetic rectangular footprint asserting the wall-top row and the roof rows. Stretch (a diagnosis that touches the roof planner); do not raise model or effort without the owner.

tasks.title: house_build: domestic chimney option (stack per house, pair or party wall) instead of one per roof unit
tasks.notes: From trial #257 (docs/plans/typology-buildings.md, "Chimneys"). house_build.roof() plans one chimney per roof unit (chim.append((best, b)): the deepest column nearest the unit's centre) and the spec has no chimney option; a terrace spec in mode group is one roof unit, so 20 houses got one chimney in the middle (owner: wrong for a terrace). feature_build's details kind chimney is only an industrial hollow stack (base_diameter at least 3), so the hand path has no domestic stack either. Add an optional per-label spec key, for example chimneys: {"<label>": "per_house" | "per_pair" | "party_walls" | [{at}] | "none"}, default per roof unit so existing specs are unchanged, placing a one-by-one brick stack on the ridge at each chosen position (party walls: where two adjacent footprints in a group share a wall line). Reuse the existing stack-through-the-roof code (WALL column to ridge + 2, flower_pot cap). Tests with synthetic fixtures: a three-house terrace and a semi. Non-builder.

tasks.title: Typology generator: glazing and facade detail as a class recipe (shopfront table into facade_plan)
tasks.notes:
From trial #257 (docs/plans/typology-buildings.md, Recommendation 4 and 5). Rule-built shops came out as plain brick boxes with the builder's default entrance and awning; the hand specs that added a facade_plan (ground storey glazed_h 3 pier 1, upper storeys glazed_h 2 pier 3, entrance with awning_like) read much closer to real shopfronts. Make glazing and facade detail (I-006) a class recipe in the typology spec generator: a small per-class table (glazing rows per storey, pier width, rhythm, entrance awning, roof edge) under the district profile or the land-use class table, emitted into the generated feature_build spec's facade_plan and roofs.edge. Houses keep the house_build windows. The recipe is a default that a profile can override, and a class with no recipe stays as today. Non-builder: fixtures and tests that the generated spec validates in feature_build (dry run on a synthetic footprint). Overlaps task 333 (shop typology: shopfront ground floor, dormers, bay windows): do the class-recipe table here and leave per-side storeys, dormers and bays to 333.


Parade verdict addition (2026-11-22, snags S-108, S-109, S-112): the class recipe also carries a sign palette (sign wood and text colour) and a per-building fascia colour; real fascias on the Portswood parade are mostly black, Burga grey and Stravs teal, not bright defaults. Per-building colour needs street-level evidence or a district profile, so the shop class stays designer-assisted. The builder options these feed are task 437 (sign wood, text colour, fascia colour, contrast rule): land 437 first. Shop typology (pitched building behind a flat shopfront) is task 333.

tasks.title: Cell-edge features: plan each feature in its primary cell
tasks.notes:
Found in trial #257 (parade, Portswood Road). Two shops straddling the 51,-37 / 52,-37 edge, ways 149855650 and 167071535, could not be built. Their feature plans were recorded under 51,-37 (when that cell's plans were recorded), but their primary cell is 52,-37. The builder then refuses them with "feature plan absent from cell plan 52,-37", and `cell_registry.py propose-features --cell 52,-37` reports no candidates for them because they are already planned elsewhere. Dismissing the plans on 51,-37 did not make 52,-37 pick them up, so they now have a plan in no cell (parade left at 17 of 19; the unbuilt two and the dismissal are described in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md under Cell edges).

Deliverable: a feature that crosses a cell edge is planned and recorded in its primary cell (the cell holding its main footprint or entrance, say which rule), whichever cell's plans were recorded first; `propose-features` for a cell lists features whose primary cell it is even when an edge cell already recorded them; recording or dismissing a plan on the other cell does not strand the feature. Fixture-only: synthetic two-cell footprint, a plan recorded in the wrong cell, then propose-features and apply preflight on the primary cell. No live world work. Acceptance: tests show the straddling feature is proposed and applies from its primary cell, and that the two-cell plan record is recoverable without a manual registry edit. After it lands, the two parade shops can be built (a separate world step, owner OK).

tasks.title: feature_build roofs: octant fit or fixed stair rotation for pitched feature roofs
tasks.notes: From trial #257 parade snag S-105 (issue I-022, docs/plans/typology-buildings.md "Parade verdict"). The owner saw poor stair rotation on the roof of Xionqi Hotpot (w122706803, hand full spec built by feature_build) and asked whether it used the octant roof system. It does not: octant exists only as house_build's roof_fit option (default columns, #415); feature_build has no octant code and its pitched roofs come from pitched_roof_states. Deliverable: decide and implement how feature_build pitched roofs get the same quality as house_build's octant fit: either accept an octant fit per roof label in the feature spec (reusing lib/builds/roof_octant.py: fit_octant_roof, block_states) or fix the stair shape and facing of pitched_roof_states against neighbours so the owner's S-105 view no longer has bad rotation; state which in the notes and why. Stretch (changes roof geometry that spans builders): ask before raising model or effort. Non-builder: fixtures that a pitched feature roof of the hotpot's footprint shape has no mismatched stair corners (compare against house_build octant output where both apply) and a validated spec option; no live world work. Acceptance: tests; roof stair rotation on that footprint verified offline; the owner reviews S-105 in game after a rebuild (a separate world step).

tasks.title: Shop signs placed illegally fall off: validate support face and write order
tasks.notes: From trial #257 parade snag S-106 (new issue I-058, "Shop signs missing or loose: placed where they can't stay"). The owner saw some shop signs that "seem to have fallen off due to illegal placement". Not yet diagnosed: signs and entities are written after the fills (McpWriter), so a wall sign whose support face is air, not solid, or overwritten by an awning or fascia block at that cell drops as an item. Deliverable: find which sign placements are illegal in the parade shops (rule-built and hand specs: w122706795 area, cell 51,-37), then make facade_plan sign placement in lib/builds/feature_build.py (and house_build if it places signs) validate the support face and the written block order: refuse or move a sign whose backing block is not solid at placement, and place signs after the blocks they hang on and after awnings. Non-builder: synthetic-footprint fixtures that every emitted sign has a solid backing block and survives the write order; a read-only live check of the parade signs is allowed to pick the cases. No live apply here. Acceptance: tests, a list of the failing parade signs with cause, and a validator that would have refused them.

tasks.title: Parade shop doors sit one level too low: diagnose and fix door floor
tasks.notes: From trial #257 parade snag S-107 (existing issue I-017, "Doors placed at the wrong height"). The owner saw shop doors "one level too low" on the Portswood Road parade (rule-built and hand-specced shops, cell 51,-37, element w122706795 area): door bottoms sit one block below the pavement. The earlier I-017 fix (#145/#146) sets the door floor against outside ground in the facade plan; this is a new case, one block not four. Deliverable: diagnose it. Read-only: for several parade shops compare the door's floor Y, the stoop/entrance step, the outside ground (lidar terrain and the live surface) and the footprint's ground level, and say which input is one block off (the facade plan's door floor, the stoop helper from #407, the ground layer's level at the shopfront, or a lowered shop floor); then fix it in the builder and add a fixture that catches it. Possible link to the ghost-ground or pavement height at shopfronts. Non-builder: no live apply, a read-only world check is allowed. Acceptance: a stated cause with numbers, a fix, and tests; the owner confirms S-107 in game after a rebuild (a separate world step).
